findings.statement: PMID:42473996 reports that CA9 is preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumor cells with low background expression in normal kidney, and that CA9-targeted PET gives proof-of-concept noninvasive discrimination of ccRCC, warranting prospective validation. High CA9 PET uptake was associated with PBRM1 loss-of-function alterations. PMID:34970493 links Ndufa4l2 to Ca9 expression in a mouse early-ccRCC model. This is a single PET study plus mechanistic mouse work, so it is proof-of-concept rather than validated. The omics ranking (rank 1) and drug records (girentuximab) agree with it.

CD70 is described as commonly overexpressed in renal cell carcinoma and minimally expressed in normal tissue, making it a potential therapeutic target (PMID:38195301). PMID:39510586 states that high, specific ccRCC expression makes it a potential diagnostic and therapeutic target. Two CD70-specific single-domain antibodies were labeled with 68Ga as radiotracers. CD70 expression is associated with overall survival in RCC patients. CD70 correlates with hypoxia pathway proteins, as a downstream target of HIF. Literature, omics, tumour-intrinsic signal and clinical-stage drugs converge here; the evidence is preclinical or early imaging and clinical work, not a validated biomarker.

ALDOB is reported as lower in ccRCC than in adjacent normal tissue by IHC (PMID:40852386). The same paper calls it a prognostic biomarker and potential immunotherapy target, and links it to Treg, Th17 and neutrophil infiltration. PMID:38655323 calls it an independent prognosis predictor in KIRC. PMID:37083815 is a pan-cancer bioinformatic analysis with low expression across cancers. ALDOB is downregulated, so a loss-of-function marker is more plausible than a drug target; the target profile for ALDOB is low. The support is mostly bioinformatic plus one IHC cohort.

PMID:41399267 reports NNMT significantly upregulated in ccRCC tumour tissue, with high expression correlating with worse overall and disease-specific survival. It calls NNMT a promising prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target, supported by transcriptomic, clinical and functional validation. PMID:37523719 describes highly selective NNMT inhibitors (II559, II802), not ccRCC-specific. Omics, TCGA prognosis and the target profile agree, but there is no clinical-stage drug.

The literature on MT1G is internally inconsistent. PMID:36204178 reports MT1G downregulated in ccRCC versus normal kidney and suggests it negatively regulates ferroptosis and marks poor prognosis. PMID:38906969 reports low MT1G in tumour tissue, yet high MT1G correlates with advanced stage and poorer prognosis, and elevated MT1G promoted growth and metastasis. The mechanism proposed is that MT1G inhibits CPT1B through H3K14 trimethylation, increasing lipid droplet accumulation. PMID:40247376 says SAP30 inhibits MT1G transcription, impairing zinc delivery to p53. Direction (tumour suppressor versus oncogenic) is unresolved, so it is a biomarker with ambiguous polarity.

PMID:36123895 reports lower SLC22A8 protein, phosphorylation and DNA methylation levels in ccRCC tissue than in normal tissue, with low methylation predicting poor overall survival. It concludes that SLC22A8 can serve as a prognostic biomarker, with survival and immune infiltration correlation. This is a single bioinformatic-plus-expression study, concordant with the omics downregulation and TCGA prognosis signals.

PMID:41158242 (pan-cancer) reports ABAT underexpressed in KIRC and other cancers and predicting poor prognosis in KIRC. PMID:41813748 reports that ABAT overexpression suppresses tumour growth in vitro and in vivo, and that ABAT mediates cGAS-STING signalling and interacts with PRMT5 to enhance interferon signalling. The in vivo functional work is not stated to be ccRCC-specific in the returned sentences. The lung adenocarcinoma migration result is not ccRCC. Vigabatrin is a known ABAT inhibitor in the drug records, but it would act against the tumour-suppressive direction suggested here, so its use is not supported.

PMID:42769428 supports an association between promoter hypermethylation and NPHS2 downregulation in ccRCC. NPHS2 loss may contribute to immune-evasive features and reduced sunitinib sensitivity. In vitro, NPHS2 overexpression suppressed malignant behaviour, attenuated EMT and weakened immune evasion. This is a single recent study and the sunitinib link is suggested only.

UMOD downregulation in ccRCC appears in three studies in the corpus. In one of them UMOD mRNA was decreased in most HIV-associated kidney cancer cases by real-time PCR, while CAIX was increased. These are descriptive expression validations of a kidney-tubule gene, with no prognostic or therapeutic claim. This looks like tissue-of-origin loss rather than a causal marker.

The only FABP1 literature in this corpus concerns colorectal and gastrointestinal adenocarcinoma (PMID:35951102): reduced expression in colorectal cancer, and an IHC marker for metastatic colorectal or GI adenocarcinoma to the lung. Nothing in the returned relations addresses FABP1 in ccRCC, so its omics rank (downregulated, with TCGA prognosis) is not literature-supported in this disease.

PIGR has Open Targets genetic association and TCGA replication, but no literature relation exists in this corpus; a sentence search returned nothing that names PIGR. Treat it as a data-only candidate.

caveats: Most literature support comes from single retrospective or bioinformatic studies (TCGA-based signatures, pan-cancer analyses); no prospective validation is reported for any gene except CA9 PET proof-of-concept needing prospective validation.
SCARB1 (rank 5) has no literature relation and the searches returned no relevant sentence, so it is a data-supported candidate with a silent literature in this corpus. PIGR likewise.
MT1G has contradictory directionality (low in tumour yet high expression linked to poor prognosis and tumour promotion).
FABP1 literature is non-ccRCC; ABAT functional sentences partly concern lung adenocarcinoma.
Downregulated genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, NPHS2, FABP1, ABAT) fit a biomarker role better than a drug-target role; the data target profile scores them low.
Only the top 12 ranked genes were reviewed because the full ranking output was too large to read.
